title: Passkeys are not a trap
author: speckx
relevanceReason: 命中 4 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: A post called Passkeys are a trap. Do not use them. has been doing the rounds over the last few days, making it pretty high on Hacker News, and I've had it sent to me many times with an 'is this true?' kind of vibe. It's written for "non-technical citizens of the web", and the headline advice is to stop using passkeys and go back to TOTP codes and passwords.The ArgumentThe post makes what appears to be one central claim: Passkeys support something called attestation, which lets a website ask for cryptographic proof of what made the passkey.The author calls this a "hidden dial" and argues that sites will slowly turn it up, until you're only allowed to log in with approved software on an approved operating system, with no modifications, no LineageOS and no sharing your Netflix password. Throw in uBlock Origin, the FIDO Alliance membership list and the UK's image-scanning proposals, and the conclusion is that passkeys are "not designed to prioritize your interests". <that-escalated-quickly.gif>It's a compelling story. It just doesn't match how any of this actually works...Your Passkeys Don't AttestThe passkeys most people use are synced passkeys, stored in iCloud Keychain, Google Password Manager, 1Password, Bitwarden or whatever other software of your choosing. These passkeys don't give websites an attestation statement at all, and though a site can ask, what comes back is none. I know this because I wrote an opensource passkeys library and made it available to everyone. If a consumer website decided tomorrow that it would only accept attested passkeys, it would lock out almost all of its own users, instantly. What website is going to do that? Besides, the guidance for consumer sites has been to not even request attestation for years now.Attestation Isn't What You Think It IsThe post describes attestation as proving "that an approved passkey manager, operating system, and firmware are in use" which is simply not true.When it is present, WebAuthn attestation tells the site the make and model of the authenticator, identified by its AAGUID, with a certificate chain from the vendor to back it up. It says nothing about your OS, your browser, your extensions, whether your phone is rooted or jailbroken, your firmware version, or even what colour it is.The YubiKey RecommendationThis is the part that surprised me the most. For people who want stronger security, the post recommends a hardware security key like a YubiKey, because it "avoids OS-wide attestation".YubiKeys are the authenticators that do attestation. Every one of them ships with a Yubico-issued attestation certificate, and enterprise attestation exists specifically so organisations can require approved hardware keys. I'd still recommend a YubiKey to anyone who wants one, they're excellent and I use them, but if attestation is the thing you're worried about, the post's own recommendation pushes you towards attestation rather than away from it!TOTP Is a Step BackwardsThe post holds up TOTP as "already" a great solution. TOTP is better than a password alone, absolutely, but it has one big weakness: you can type the code into the wrong website, just ask my good friend Troy Hunt. Phishing kits like Evilginx sit in the middle, relay your password and code to the real site in real time, and walk away with your session. This isn't theoretical, it's how a huge number of account takeovers happen today and we have the evidence to prove it. This is the problem that passkeys solve. A passkey is bound to the domain it was created for, so your browser simply won't use your example.com passkey on examp1e.com. There's no code to read out and nothing for the user to get wrong. The author even concedes this in the addendum, saying that passkeys are domain-bound and resist man-in-the-middle attacks, but still tells readers to avoid them. Swapping a phishing-resistant credential for a phishable one is a really bad trade...What You Should DoKeep using passkeys! Wherever a site offers one, take it, and store it in a password/passkey manager you trust. If you want to be able to move your credentials around, pick a provider that supports that. If you're worried about attestation creeping into consumer logins, then that's worth pushing back on, loudly (if it ever happens). But it hasn't happened, the biggest providers don't support it, and avoiding passkeys today while you wait for it won't protect you from anything, it just leaves you open to phishing.SourcesI have some experience in this area:I created WhyNoPasskeys.com to track the availability of passkeys on the Web. I built and deployed passkeys support on my own SaaS company.We built our own passkeys library and had it security reviewed.I wrote about Security considerations when using Passkeys on your website.I wrote Passkeys 101: An Introduction to Passkeys and How They Work.I made our passkeys library opensource for everyone to use.I've done extensive security testing of passkeys implementations. I've openly acknowledged the limitations of not using attestation on passkeys.I think most of all that it's important to say I use passkeys everywhere I can because they're currently the best thing we have available to protect our accounts. And they're not a trap. comments.author: bonzog
comments.textRawHtml:
I don't know enough to argue about whether passkeys are a trap or not, but I do know as a user that they appear to be a confusing mess.

When a website prompts me to set up a passkey, depending on the device I happen to be using at the time it could end up going to Google password manager, Samsung password manager, iCloud Keychain, or Windows somethingorother.

What happens when I go to the same site on a different platform? What if I can't use cross-device authentication because I'm on a locked-down work machine or one that simply doesn't have bluetooth? What if I want to consolidate them all in one platform just for the sake of being organised? What if I lose or simply don't have the device with a certain passkey near me?

I don't have the time or patience to work out any of that, which might absolutely be a 'me' problem, but TOTPs are pretty sodding frictionless in comparison. Scan QR in my chosen manager; type number into website; done. Why are passkeys better?
comments.textZhHtml:
我没有足够的知识去争论万能钥匙是否是一个陷阱，但作为一个用户，我确实知道万能钥匙似乎是一个令人困惑的混乱。

当网站提示我设置万能钥匙时，根据我当时使用的设备，它最终可能会转到 Google 密码管理器、三星密码管理器、iCloud 钥匙串或 Windows 等。

当我在不同的网站上访问同一网站时会发生什么情况平台？如果我因为使用​​的是锁定的工作计算机或根本没有蓝牙而无法使用跨设备身份验证怎么办？如果我只是为了组织起来而想将它们全部整合到一个平台上怎么办？如果我丢失了或者根本没有带有特定密钥的设备在我身边怎么办？

我没有时间或耐心来解决这些问题，这绝对是“我”的问题，但相比之下，TOTP 非常无摩擦。扫描我选择的经理中的二维码；在网站中输入号码；完毕。为什么密钥更好？

children.author: chaboud
children.textRawHtml:
I thought "Passkeys are a trap" was going to be about this usability nightmare. Some sites, once connected via passkey, make it all but impossible to connect in another way. Some support multiple passkeys. Some do not. Some support passkey or something else. Some do not.

The idea and protocol are pretty solid, though we're back to a "biometrics as password" problem in many device flows, but every time I'm urged by a site to convert to a passkey, I wonder "is this site the sort that would screw this up?"

So far, it's about 30% of sites screwing it up...
children.textZhHtml:
我认为“密钥是一个陷阱”将是关于这个可用性噩梦的。有些网站一旦通过密钥连接，就几乎不可能以其他方式连接。有些支持多个密钥。有些则不然。 有些支持密钥或其他东西。有些则不然。

这个想法和协议非常可靠，尽管我们在许多设备流程中又回到了“生物识别作为密码”的问题，但每次网站敦促我转换为密钥时，我都想知道“这个网站是那种会把事情搞砸的网站吗？”

到目前为止，大约有 30% 的网站搞砸了......

children.author: gortok
children.textRawHtml:
This is the issue.

I can’t adopt Passkeys if I’m not certain they’re going to work as well as my password manager and Authenticator app, which is to say 100% of the time.

When sites ask to set up passkeys, it’s usually native passkeys (especially on iOS). And figuring out how to get the flow to set up a LastPass key by default seems unusually difficult.

I also use a MacBook, windows desktop, an iPhone and iPad. I use Firefox, edge, brave across these devices.

When I say “passkeys are a trap” they are a usability trap where no one can attest with certainty that I won’t wake up in a painful situation because I decided to adopt passkeys.
children.textZhHtml:
这就是问题所在。

如果我不确定密钥能否像我的密码管理器和身份验证器应用程序一样工作（也就是说 100% 成功），我就不能采用密钥。

当网站要求设置密钥时，通常是本机密钥（尤其是在 iOS 上）。弄清楚如何在默认情况下设置 LastPass 密钥的流程似乎异常困难。

我还使用 MacBook、Windows 台式机、iPhone 和 iPad。我在这些设备上使用 Firefox、edge、brave。

当我说“密钥是一个陷阱”时，它们是一个可用性陷阱，没有人可以肯定地证明我不会因为我决定采用密钥而在痛苦的情况中醒来。

children.author: jasomill
children.textRawHtml:
It's ironic that passkeys are most usable in conjunction with a password manager that syncs them across all of a user's devices, but this is also the scenario where they have the least security benefit over traditional passwords.

I do appreciate that passkey adoption has led to wider support for hardware security tokens for sites where I actually care about increased security over password managers, however.
children.textZhHtml:
具有讽刺意味的是，万能钥匙最适合与在所有用户设备上同步万能钥匙的密码管理器结合使用，但这也是它们相对于传统密码的安全优势最小的情况。

我确实很欣赏万能钥匙的采用导致了对硬件安全令牌的更广泛支持，但我实际上关心的是比密码管理器更高的安全性。

children.author: solyin
children.textRawHtml: The specific security benefit is that there's no way for a tech-stupid person, or a tech-literate person who's short on sleep, to copy paste their password into p4ypal.com instead of PayPal.com.
children.textZhHtml: 具体的安全优势是，技术笨的人或睡眠不足的技术高手无法将其密码复制粘贴到 p4ypal.com 而不是 PayPal.com。

children.author: Dylan16807
children.textRawHtml:
Yes but if you have a password manager that's set up well you'll never be copy pasting passwords in the first place. If the password doesn't show up you know there's a problem.

The benefit of a passkey here isn't zero but it's at the minimum.
children.textZhHtml:
是的，但是如果您有一个设置良好的密码管理器，您将永远不会首先复制粘贴密码。 如果密码没有显示，您就知道存在问题。

此处密钥的好处不是零，而是最低限度。

children.author: thayne
children.textRawHtml: This would be true if websites consistently annotated inputs correctly, but they don't. So password managers are left to guess what input is the username, which is the password, etc. and they don't always get it right.
children.textZhHtml: 如果网站始终正确地注释输入，则情况确实如此，但事实并非如此。因此，密码管理器只能猜测输入的用户名、密码等，但他们并不总是能猜对。

children.author: nh2
children.textRawHtml:
> for a tech-stupid person

> password doesn't show up you know there's a problem

Here is your contradiction.

The normal person will just assume that some tech isn't working today again.

A key point of passkeys seems to be that it guarantees to the site owner that the user cannot be phished, without having to make assumptions on whether the user is tech-stupid.
children.textZhHtml:
> 对于技术愚蠢的人

> 密码不显示，你知道有问题

这就是你的矛盾。

普通人只会假设今天某些技术又不起作用了。

万能钥匙的一个关键点似乎是它向网站所有者保证用户不会被网络钓鱼，而不必假设用户是否是网络钓鱼的技术愚蠢。

children.author: Brian_K_White
children.textRawHtml:
"it guarantees to the site owner that the user cannot be phished"

Well gee how nice for the site owner.

Problem is my priorities are my absolute ability to never lose my most critical assets through some means outside my control, not the site's convenience.

It was ok to use imperfect systems back in the days when the bank and the store and even the government all had a desk a mile away you could go to in person and get anything cleared up and override all possible "usually it works like this" with your physical presense an drivers licence and birth certificate or simply 5 people who all attest they know you.

We no longer have that ultimate backup plan, so really F anyone's attempt to justify basically tricking people into doing something unwise that puts them at actually greater risk because their life is less under their own control, and doing this under the very banner of claiming to care about the users safety!

It's freaking amazing.
children.textZhHtml:
“它向网站所有者保证用户不会被网络钓鱼”

好吧，这对网站所有者来说多好。

问题是我的首要任务是我绝对有能力永远不会通过我无法控制的某种方式失去我最重要的资产，而不是网站的便利性。

在银行、商店甚至政府都在一英里外设有办公桌的日子里，使用不完善的系统是可以的。亲自去清理一切并覆盖所有可能的“通常是这样的”，用你的身体在场，驾驶执照和出生证明，或者只是五个人都证明他们认识你。

我们不再有那个最终的后备计划，所以任何人都试图证明基本上欺骗人们做一些不明智的事情，这实际上使他们面临更大的风险，因为他们的生活不太受自己的控制，并且在声称关心用户的旗帜下这样做安全！

太棒了。

children.author: trinsic2
children.textRawHtml: This is the rub for me. Passkeys are really about protecting the site and not the user. Its really designed backwards IMHO.
children.textZhHtml: 这对我来说是个难题。密钥实际上是为了保护站点而不是用户。恕我直言，它的设计确实是向后的。

children.author: Dylan16807
children.textRawHtml: I don't know if they'd even be aware of how to copy the password out of the manager...
children.textZhHtml: 我不知道他们是否知道如何从管理器中复制密码...

children.author: kergonath
children.textRawHtml: They have to be, because quite regularly password managers fail to detect properly user name or password fields, in which case you have to copy and paste by hand.
children.textZhHtml: 它们必须如此，因为密码管理器经常无法正确检测用户名或密码字段，在这种情况下您必须手动复制和粘贴。

children.author: Dylan16807
children.textRawHtml:
I've had that happen to me less often than sites simply being broken. If I couldn't copy-paste I'd be fine.

If someone only ever saved passwords from the browser UI they really could have no idea how to manually copy a password, while getting along fine.
children.textZhHtml:
我遇到这种情况的次数比网站被破坏的次数还要少。 如果我无法复制粘贴，那就没问题了。

如果有人只从浏览器 UI 保存密码，他们真的不知道如何手动复制密码，同时相处得很好。

children.author: vel0city
children.textRawHtml:
I've used a number of password managers over decades. I'm still having to copy and paste passwords from time to time due to poor/hostile website designs, needing to authenticate into a browser/app that doesn't have the plugin configured yet, bugginess on the plugin detecting the right site, etc. And in the end, if the user can copy and paste that wherever, the user will copy and paste that wherever.

Meanwhile there are other security benefits as well. With a password, that static credential is transmitted in the handshake. It can be mishandled somewhere in between, and now that entire root credential is potentially compromised. This is just impossible with a passkey. The credential never leaves the client. In some implementations, the credential never leaves a secure enclave, never even entering the client's system memory. You can't say the same for passwords, not even close.
children.textZhHtml:
几十年来我使用过许多密码管理器。由于糟糕/恶意的网站设计，需要对尚未配置插件的浏览器/应用程序进行身份验证，检测正确站点的插件存在错误等，我仍然不得不时不时地复制和粘贴密码。最后，如果用户可以将其复制并粘贴到任何地方，那么用户将将其复制并粘贴到任何地方。

同时还有其他安全优势。使用密码时，该静态凭证将在握手中传输。它可能会在两者之间的某个地方处理不当，现在整个根凭证可能会受到损害。这对于密钥来说是不可能的。凭证永远不会离开客户。在一些实现中，凭证永远不会离开安全飞地，甚至永远不会进入客户端的系统内存。对于密码，你不能说同样的话，甚至不是很接近。

children.author: fiddlerwoaroof
children.textRawHtml: Yeah, a lot of websites these days seem to block or mess up autofill where I actually want it: I can’t say how many websites break credit card autocomplete, TOTP code autocomplete (e.g. via Apple’s native TOTP implementation), username/password autocomplete. I can never really tell if it’s incompetence or a misguided idea of security, but it’s extremely annoying.
children.textZhHtml: 是的，现在很多网站似乎在我真正想要的地方阻止或搞乱了自动填充：我无法说出有多少网站破坏了信用卡自动完成、TOTP 代码自动完成（例如通过 Apple 的本机 TOTP 实现）、用户名/密码自动完成。我永远无法真正判断这是无能还是错误的安全观念，但这非常烦人。

children.author: kccqzy
children.textRawHtml:
> I do appreciate that passkey adoption has led to wider support for hardware security tokens

In my experience this simply didn’t happen. Many sites support passkeys but only the native passkey stored on the current device, but not a hardware security key. Many sites don’t even allow multiple passkeys, which is frankly required if you use hardware security because you will want multiple pieces of hardware in case one is misplaced.
children.textZhHtml:
> 我确实很欣赏密钥的采用带来了对硬件安全令牌的更广泛支持

根据我的经验，这根本没有发生。许多站点支持密钥，但仅支持当前设备上存储的本机密钥，而不支持硬件安全密钥。许多网站甚至不允许使用多个万能钥匙，坦率地说，如果您使用硬件安全性，这是必需的，因为您将需要多个硬件，以防其中一个丢失。

children.author: rlpb
children.textRawHtml:
> Many sites support passkeys but only the native passkey stored on the current device, but not a hardware security key.

That's a function of your browser, not the site.

Your point about multiple passkeys is valid though. That affects me too. I use multiple hardware keys but cannot enroll many sites because of this.
children.textZhHtml:
> 许多网站支持密钥，但仅支持当前设备上存储的本机密钥，而不是硬件安全密钥。

这是浏览器的功能，而不是网站的功能。

不过，您关于多个密钥的观点是有效的。这也影响着我。我使用多个硬件密钥，但因此无法注册许多站点。

children.author: nine_k
children.textRawHtml:
> that syncs them across all of a user's devices

What's the point of a passkey that can technically be exfiltrated off a device it was created on? I thought the whole premise of passkeys is that they can't be copied, and hence can be trusted as much as the device access control. Am I missing something?
children.textZhHtml:
> 在用户的所有设备上同步它们

从技术上讲可以从创建它的设备上泄露的密钥有什么意义？我认为万能钥匙的整个前提是它们无法被复制，因此可以像设备访问控制一样值得信任。我错过了什么吗？

children.author: xp84
children.textRawHtml:
It would introduce a different usability problem to have them remain truly stuck on a device, like, locked inside a Secure Enclave. Mainly that you’d have to do the setup again for every website, on every device. Buy a new phone? Back to the Stone Age. Authenticate with a password to each site on the new device, find the “add passkey” place, and install it.

I think that is a big step down from the convenience and friction level that the native password managers get you, where you save your password once and for the rest of your life, as long as you maintain fealty to Apple/Google/Microsoft, your password will always be there in autofill.
children.textZhHtml:
让它们真正卡在设备上（例如锁定在安全区域内）会带来不同的可用性问题。主要是您必须在每台设备上为每个网站重新进行设置。买新手机？回到石器时代。在新设备上使用每个站点的密码进行身份验证，找到“添加密钥”位置，然后安装它。

我认为这与本机密码管理器为您带来的便利性和摩擦程度相比是一个很大的进步，在本机密码管理器中，您可以一次性保存密码并终身使用，只要您保持对 Apple/Google/Microsoft 的忠诚，您的密码将始终在自动填充中。
